compute_scorecard (report.rs:118-149) and render_evidence_by_lane (report.rs:255-307) each independently rebuild the fact_ids BTreeSet lookup from packet.trusted_facts and independently reimplement the fact:{id} promotion check (:134+140 vs :256+277) instead of sharing one is_promoted helper. This copy-paste duplication is the direct mechanism that let the two implementations silently diverge on the kind exclusion - nothing in the code forces them to agree. A single shared predicate would make 'asserted' a compile-time single source of truth.

Coverage math (report.rs:151-173) is per-spec, not a builder deviation, but worth flagging for founder-readability: the denominator lumps verifier-tier facts (some evidentiary weight) with asserted evidence (no proof) as equally not-attested; the raw counts beside the percentage are the only place that distinction survives, styled as smaller secondary text. Flagging for Prime's awareness only.

Verified the four correctness risk classes named in the review brief and found no defects: (1) escaping - html_escape (report.rs:35-48) applied at all ~24 call sites incl. href attributes (:221-222); (2) division by zero - denom==0 guarded at :154-156; (3) unwraps - zero .unwrap() in report.rs, Option access via as_deref/unwrap_or with safe defaults; (4) Windows paths - receipt links (:213-223) are hardcoded forward-slash literals, never Path::display, so hrefs cannot emit backslashes.
